title: Rabbi Yochanan ben Dehavai (a Tanna of a Baraita)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Rabbi Yehudah ben Teima, as in [Sanhedrin 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.4b.15), where he said in his name that one blind in one eye is exempt from appearing [at the Temple]. The statement is cited in [Chagigah 2a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.2a.6) and [Arakhin 2b](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.2b.12), and there it is Rabbi Yehudah without further designation, but Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Yehudah ben Teima. In [Menachot 42b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.42b.14) he disagrees with Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel concerning tekhelet.

An aggadic saying of his remains to us in [Nedarim 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.20a.13), where he said: “The ministering angels told me four things: why are there lame people,” etc. In [Avot deRabbi Natan 27](https://www.sefaria.org/Avot_DeRabbi_Natan.27.3), he says: “Whoever says that the halakhah was not created (or: is not fitting) has no share in the world to come.” He said there: “Do not distance yourself from a measure that has no limit, nor from a labor that has no end,” and he told a fine parable about this.[^2]

notes.text: The alternative נראית is rendered fitting, not given; saved Vilna Avot deRabbi Natan27 has נבראת. These are alternative readings recorded by Hyman, not a new emendation of the source.

Sanhedrin gives the full name Yehudah ben Teima; Chagigah and Arakhin have Yehudah without that qualification. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1823&lang=en) records the difference. The linked Avot deRabbi Natan gives נבראת, “was created,” and follows the saying with the parable of carrying water from the sea to dry land.
